The record:
Write the overview of the executive synopsis for the incident on io-shop below: a short paragraph in plain words, for the people who lead the company rather than the engineers who responded - what happened, how long it lasted, what it cost the business and the people who responded, and how it was resolved.

What a reader saw: Shoppers' account pages failed to load
Why, in plain words: Someone turned off a setting that kept account pages on their older version, which sent shoppers to a newer version that likely breaks when it works out an average of this month's spending for anyone who has bought nothing this month.

Figures:
- How long it lasted: 13m 0s {duration}
- Requests failing at the worst minute: 37.5% {peak_error_rate}
- What it cost the shop in takings (estimated by Argus): 8,241.24 USD {customer_loss}
- Nobody was paged: no on-call incident was linked to this one.

What was done to end it:
- Argus: reverted the feature flag monthly-spend-feature - refuted, put back when it did not help
- Argus: reverted the feature flag legacy-checkout-fallback - confirmed, still in place
- Argus: proposed a fix, PR #525 - opened as a draft

Name {duration} and {customer_loss} in your overview.
Write no figure yourself - not in digits, not spelled out, and not as a word that sizes it ("a brief outage", "a minor loss", "tripled"). Where a figure goes, write its name, braces and all, and the synopsis writes the figure in.
Say nothing about how the incident was resolved beyond what the list of what was done says: a draft fix has not run, and nothing it would do has happened.
Speak of Argus by name, never as "we", "our" or "us": Argus is the system that responded, and each line of what was done says who did it.
Where you say who was affected, say which ones, as the cause does, or that some were, where it does not say which - never how many, and never all of them, where the cause does not say all.
Keep "likely" on what the cause says is likely, and only there.

Call submit_executive_overview with your overview.

The postmortem it is written from:
Shoppers' account pages failed to load while legacy-checkout-fallback was off
Incident: HighErrorRate on io-shop
Date: Nov 11, 2026, 01:58 to 02:11 UTC
Status: Draft. 1 of 6 action items are done.
Written by: Argus Postmortem agent, Nov 11, 2026, 02:19:08 UTC. Not reviewed yet. Each part is as of when the work it reports ended, which the timeline dates; who ended the incident is as of now.
First told: Argus posted in Slack, Nov 11, 2026, 02:05:48 UTC
Ended by: Argus: reverted the feature flag legacy-checkout-fallback - confirmed, still in place

Summary
The service broke at 01:58 UTC and was back to normal at 02:11 UTC, 13 minutes later. 29.5% of requests failed while it was broken, against 1.0% before it began. At its worst, 37.5% failed. The shop's takings fell short of the same hours on earlier weeks by 8,241.24 USD, beyond how much those hours vary on their own. Someone turned off a setting that kept account pages on their older version, which sent shoppers to a newer version that likely breaks when it works out an average of this month's spending for anyone who has bought nothing this month. What Argus did: reverted the feature flag monthly-spend-feature (can be put back) - refuted, put back when it did not help; reverted the feature flag legacy-checkout-fallback (can be put back) - confirmed, still in place. Argus opened a draft fix, PR #525, for a person to review and merge. If legacy-checkout-fallback is switched off again, the new renderer would serve account pages again, and they would fail for shoppers who have bought nothing this month.

Impact
13m 0s - onset until back to normal
37.5% - peak error rate
4,596 - requests failed
1.0% to 29.5% - what the alert watches, before onset and while broken on average (the rule's line is 10%)
8,241.24 USD - customer loss (estimated)

Root cause and contributing factors
Switching legacy-checkout-fallback off sent account pages to the new renderer, and those pages reach average_spend_per_item_this_month in src/io_shop/spend_summary.py. Code-Fix read that function as dividing this month's spend total by the number of purchases made this month, with nothing to handle a month with no purchases. So for any shopper who has bought before but not this month, the division raises ZeroDivisionError and the account page fails. It rests on F1, a reading of the source nothing ran, so it is unverified.
Causal chain
symptom Shoppers' account pages failed: account page requests came back as failed pages, and the logged account-page error rate peaked at 02:02 UTC.
  Evidence:
    G5309 ERROR io-shop: account page request failed - ZeroDivisionError: division by zero at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47 - 16 occurrences in 8 minutes, 01:58–02:05
    Gbac1 WARN io-shop: account page error rate at #% over the last minute - 32 occurrences in 38 minutes, 01:28–02:05; # was 0.50% to 35.00%, typically 1.50%, highest at 02:02
why 1 Account page requests raised a ZeroDivisionError at line 47 of src/io_shop/spend_summary.py over 01:58–02:05 UTC, and each request that raised it failed.
  Evidence:
    G5309
why 2 At 01:58:33 UTC the flag legacy-checkout-fallback was switched off, and account pages moved from the legacy renderer to the new one. At 01:58 UTC, 83 of the flag's evaluations read off. Over 01:59–02:05 UTC every evaluation read off. The new renderer's count of account pages served was highest at 01:59 UTC, after being typically 0 before.
  Evidence:
    P1 01:58:33 UTC flag toggle legacy-checkout-fallback by admin: feature flag legacy-checkout-fallback was switched off
    G7ad6 INFO io-shop: legacy-checkout-fallback=off 83 / on 117 - 200 evaluations - 1 occurrence in 1 minute, 01:58
    G7037 INFO io-shop: legacy-checkout-fallback=off - 200 evaluations - 7 occurrences in 7 minutes, 01:59–02:05
    Gc27d INFO io-shop: account pages served - # by the legacy renderer, # by the new renderer - 38 occurrences in 38 minutes, 01:28–02:05; # was 0 to 200, typically 200, highest at 01:28; # was 0 to 200, typically 0, highest at 01:59
  Ruled out:
    The switch-on of monthly-spend-feature at 01:58:33 UTC, made at the same instant (candidate C1). Turning that flag back off left the service at the incident's level, so the flag was put back on.
      T17 02:07:25 Mitigation Agent: Reverted the feature flag monthly-spend-feature for C1, moved from ON to OFF
      T19 02:09:02 Mitigation Agent: Looked at the service - still at the incident's level
      T20 02:10:25 Mitigation Agent: Judged the action REFUTED - monthly-spend-feature was put back ON
    A deploy or release on the service: the Investigator Agent asked for production change events - deploys, releases and flag changes on the service, the 1 day 1 minute before Nov 11 01:59; the Investigator Agent read back 2 production changes. A rollout still under way: the Investigator Agent read how far the deployment had rolled out - all 3 replicas run one revision, which the history does not name.
      T7
      T8
      T9
why 3 Pages served by the new renderer reach average_spend_per_item_this_month, which, as Code-Fix reads it, divides by the number of purchases made this month and so fails for any shopper who has bought nothing this month.
  Evidence:
    F1 What Code-Fix read in the source and proposed - nothing ran its test or its fix
    G5309
    Gc27d
Contributing factors
- Before legacy-checkout-fallback was switched off in production, no check was seen that the new renderer serves an account with past purchases but none this month. (AI-3)
- The flag change moved all account-page traffic to the new renderer at once. Every evaluation read off from the minute after the switch, and no staged rollout or automatic halt on rising errors was seen. (AI-4)
- legacy-checkout-fallback and monthly-spend-feature were changed by the same admin at the same instant, and the error named the spend-summary code. That made it hard to tell which change caused the failures. (AI-5)

Hypotheses considered
 | Hypothesis | Confidence | Result
C1 | At 01:58:33 UTC the feature flag monthly-spend-feature was switched on. Account page requests then began failing with ZeroDivisionError at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47, taking the error rate from about 1% to about 34%. No deployment was involved, the rollout converged, and latency and resources stayed flat. | 0.55 | refuted
C2 | At 01:58:33 UTC the feature flag legacy-checkout-fallback was switched off. Account pages moved from the legacy renderer to the new renderer, which raises the ZeroDivisionError. The new-renderer count at 01:58 (83) equals the flag's off-evaluation count (83). | 0.38 | confirmed

Trigger
legacy-checkout-fallback flag went from ON to OFF at 01:58:33 UTC, by admin.

Resolution
 | Time (UTC) | Action | By | Kind | Outcome
M1 | 02:07:25 | Reverted the feature flag monthly-spend-feature for C1 | Argus | can be put back | refuted, put back when it did not help
M2 | 02:10:35 | Reverted the feature flag legacy-checkout-fallback for C2 | Argus | can be put back | confirmed, still in place
 | 02:13:42 | Proposed a fix: PR #525 | Code-Fix Agent | nothing to put back | opened as a draft

Detection
The incident on io-shop began at 01:58 UTC. HighErrorRate fired at 02:05:23 UTC, 7 minutes 23 seconds later.
What the alert said
AL1 | Error rate above threshold for 5m

Action items
Item | Action | Type | Owner | Tracking | Status
AI-1 | Reverted the feature flag legacy-checkout-fallback | mitigate | Argus | - | done
AI-2 | Review and merge the proposed fix | prevent | unassigned | PR #525 | open
AI-3 | Before a flag is switched in production, require a test run of the code path it turns on. For legacy-checkout-fallback, that means the new renderer serving an account with past purchases but none this month. | prevent | unassigned | - | open
AI-4 | Roll out flag changes that move account pages between renderers in stages, with an automatic halt and revert when the account-page error rate rises. | prevent | unassigned | - | open
AI-5 | Make production flag changes on io-shop one at a time, with enough time between them to tell their effects apart. | process | unassigned | - | open
AI-6 | Link the HighErrorRate alert on io-shop to an on-call rotation so that a person is paged when it fires. | detect | unassigned | - | open

Lessons learned
What went well
- The alert came within the 7 minutes 30 seconds accounted for by its rule waiting 5 minutes with its condition holding, its evaluation at intervals of 1 minute, an unmeasured allowance of 30 seconds for scraping and storing its samples and the whole minute the onset is measured to.
- 45 seconds after the alert was raised, the Investigator Agent placed the start of the incident at 01:58.
- 1 minute 50 seconds after the alert was raised, Argus read the flag provider's history - 2 flag changes by anyone but Argus, the 1 hour before 02:07:12.
- 5 minutes 2 seconds after the alert was raised, the Mitigation Agent judged the action REFUTED - monthly-spend-feature was put back ON.
- 5 minutes 12 seconds after the alert was raised, the Mitigation Agent reverted the feature flag legacy-checkout-fallback for C2, moved from OFF to ON.
- 8 minutes 19 seconds after the alert was raised, the Code-Fix Agent proposed a fix as a draft pull request - PR #525.
What went wrong
- Nobody was paged. No on-call incident was linked to the alert, so no person was called in to work it.
- The investigation ranked monthly-spend-feature above legacy-checkout-fallback because the error named the spend-summary code, so the first revert went to the wrong flag. Yet the new renderer's count at the onset matched the fallback flag's off evaluations, and the thread had named the fallback flag.
Where it got lucky
Nothing.

What people told Argus

What Code-Fix read in the source and proposed - nothing ran its test or its fix
F1 | The fault: average_spend_per_item_this_month in src/io_shop/spend_summary.py ends with account.total_this_month_cents // len(bought_this_month) (line 47, the line the ZeroDivisionError names). bought_this_month holds only the purchases flagged in_current_month, so for any shopper who has bought before but not this month the list is empty and the division raises. The tests already describe that shopper as the ordinary case. Any account page that reaches this figure fails at the request boundary in src/io_shop/account_page.py, which records the error and returns a failed page. Turning the flag off stopped traffic reaching this path but did not fix the arithmetic, so turning it back on would bring the failures straight back.

The change: when nothing was bought this month, the function returns 0. That is the true figure: the shopper has spent nothing per item this month. Otherwise the calculation is unchanged. The lifetime average, render_spend_summary and the boundary's broad catch are untouched. The existing test that the lifetime path still raises for an account with no purchases at all still holds, so failures elsewhere are not hidden.

The test: tests/io_shop/test_spend_summary.py gains cases that call average_spend_per_item_this_month directly, and render_spend_summary(..., use_monthly_summary=True), on an account with past purchases but none this month. Both expect 0. Against the current code both calls raise ZeroDivisionError.
Assumptions
- Exchange rate: EUR converted at 0.92191 per USD, published 2026-11-10
- No engineer minutes: no on-call incident was linked to this one, so nobody was paged to respond

Review checklist
✓ Key incident data collected (met)
✓ Impact assessed (met)
○ Root-cause analysis complete (for a person)
  running the proposed fix's tests against the current code would confirm the reading, not that the code it reads is what ran (AI-2)
○ Every action item owned and dated (for a person)
○ Reviewed and shared (for a person)

The document, by field:
overview: For {duration}, some shoppers on io-shop could not load their account pages, and at the worst minute {peak_error_rate} of requests failed. Someone had turned off a setting that kept account pages on their older version. That sent shoppers to a newer version that likely breaks when it works out an average of this month's spending for anyone who has bought nothing this month. Argus estimates the shop lost {customer_loss} in takings. Nobody was paged, so the incident took no on-call time. Argus responded. It first turned off a different setting, monthly-spend-feature, but that did not help, so Argus switched it back. Argus then turned the account-page setting, legacy-checkout-fallback, back on. That ended the failures, and the setting is still on. Argus has also proposed a code fix, but it is only a draft and has not been applied.

Not to be judged:
  - Names in braces, such as {duration}, are figures code writes in from the list of figures in the ask. They are not judged.
  - The overview is written in plain words for the people who lead the company. A claim said more plainly than the postmortem says it is grounded where it means the same.

Judge every claim in the document, and answer by calling judge_claims.

tools.description: Submit every claim in the document, each either as supported or as flagged. Supported: the document's own words, quoted exactly, and the record's rows that support it. Flagged: the document's own words, quoted exactly, why, and the record's rows that contradict it (none where no row speaks to it at all). Empty lists say the document makes no claim to judge.

why.description: One sentence: what the record holds instead. Never empty.
